card-model.instruction:
Read docs/TASK_P1_cards.md FIRST: section 2.2 is the contract (the types of src/cards/types.ts verbatim, every fault message as an exact string, the order of faults), section 2.3 the names, section 4 the constraints. docs/CONVENTIONS.md is the style of the tree.

Write three files and nothing else: src/cards/types.ts (exactly the types of section 2.2, no values), src/cards/model.ts (validateCard(input: unknown): CardResult and loadDeck(text: string): DeckResult, importing its types with `import type { ... } from "./types.js"`, node:path for normalisation, no node:fs, no process, no Date), and tests/cards/model.test.ts, a SMOKE test only: at most five test(...) calls (an import, one happy path per function on tests/fixtures/decks/tiny.json via fixture() from ../helpers.js, one tolerant case), toBe on scalars and short strings. The judge writes the example tests, not you. Every message string in the table of section 2.2 is copied exactly, the key order of faults is the schema order, and all faults come back at once.

card-model-judge.instruction: You write tests/cards/model.examples.test.ts only. Import validateCard and loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js", types from "../../src/cards/types.js", and fixture/fixtureJson from "../helpers.js"; the fixtures named in section 2.1 of docs/TASK_P1_cards.md hold every example's input (tests/fixtures/cards/*.json for single cards, tests/fixtures/decks/*.json for decks). One test(...) per example below, in this order, named `<Function> example <n>`; then at most twelve tests of your own on the rules of section 2.2. Compare faults as faults.length, faults[0].key and faults[0].message with toBe against the exact strings of section 2.2; narrow a CardResult with `if (!r.ok) ...` and fail with expect.unreachable, never with a cast. Write no file anywhere (loadDeck takes text, not a path).

layering.instruction: Read docs/TASK_P1_cards.md section 2.2 (layerGenerations) and 2.3. Write two files and nothing else: src/cards/layer.ts exporting layerGenerations(deck: Deck): string[][] (types via `import type { Deck } from "./types.js"`; no node:* imports needed; a cycle in a hand-built Deck throws an Error whose message starts with `dependsOn cycle`), and tests/cards/layer.test.ts, a SMOKE test only: at most five test(...) calls, building a Deck with loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js" on fixture("decks/layered.json") from "../helpers.js", comparing JSON.stringify of the result with toBe. The judge writes the example tests, not you.

layering-judge.instruction: You write tests/cards/layer.examples.test.ts only. Build each Deck with loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js" on fixture("decks/layered.json") and fixture("decks/layeredExternal.json") from "../helpers.js" (narrow with `if (!r.ok) expect.unreachable(...)`), call layerGenerations from "../../src/cards/layer.js", and compare JSON.stringify(result) with toBe against the record's literal written exactly as `[["a"],["b","c"],["d"]]` and `[["a","b"]]`. One test(...) per example below, in this order, named `Layer Generations example <n>`; then at most twelve tests of your own on section 2.2 (empty deck, the cycle throw). Write no file anywhere.

weigh.instruction: Read docs/TASK_P1_cards.md section 2.2 (weighSlices) and 2.3. Write two files and nothing else: src/cards/weigh.ts exporting weighSlices(deck: Deck, root: string, cap = 500000): Weighing (types via `import type { Deck, Hazard, SliceWeight, Weighing } from "./types.js"`; node:fs statSync and node:path join only; root is always the parameter, never process.cwd()), and tests/cards/weigh.test.ts, a SMOKE test only: at most five test(...) calls, using tmpRoot() from "../helpers.js" to write files of known size (tmpRoot().write(rel, text) returns the absolute path; rm() at the end) and loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js" to build the Deck, comparing bytes and hazards.length with toBe. The judge writes the example tests, not you.

weigh-judge.instruction: You write tests/cards/weigh.examples.test.ts only. For the 600001-byte example: r = tmpRoot() from "../helpers.js", r.write("big.txt", "x".repeat(600001)), a Deck from loadDeck ("../../src/cards/model.js") of one card with targets ["big.txt"], weighSlices(deck, r.root) from "../../src/cards/weigh.js", then r.rm(); assert hazards.length, kind, severity, bytes and cap with toBe against 600001 and 500000. tests/fixtures/decks/weigh.json weighed with root = the repository root (path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "../..")) gives bytes 110, missing ["tests/fixtures/weigh/missing.txt"], no hazard; with cap 100 one hazard (bytes 110, cap 100). One test(...) per example below, in this order, named `Weigh Slices example <n>`; then at most twelve tests of your own on section 2.2. Write only under tmpRoot() and remove it.

hazards.instruction: Read docs/TASK_P1_cards.md section 2.2 (findHazards: the four kinds, their fields, their order) and 2.3. Write two files and nothing else: src/cards/hazards.ts exporting findHazards(deck: Deck): Hazard[] (types via `import type { Deck, Hazard } from "./types.js"`, generations via `import { layerGenerations } from "./layer.js"`; no node:* imports; bytes and cap are never set here), and tests/cards/hazards.test.ts, a SMOKE test only: at most five test(...) calls, building Decks with loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js" on fixture("decks/hazardsWriteWrite.json") and fixture("decks/hazardsReadWrite.json") from "../helpers.js", comparing hazards.length, kind and path with toBe. The judge writes the example tests, not you.

hazards-judge.instruction: You write tests/cards/hazards.examples.test.ts only. Build each Deck with loadDeck from "../../src/cards/model.js" on fixture("decks/hazardsWriteWrite.json") and fixture("decks/hazardsReadWrite.json") from "../helpers.js" (narrow with `if (!r.ok) expect.unreachable(...)`), call findHazards from "../../src/cards/hazards.js", and assert hazards.length with toBe(1) and then kind, severity, path, cards.join(",") and JSON.stringify(repair) with toBe, each against the literal of the example (repair of the read-write example is {"addDependsOn":{"card":"b","on":"a"}}). One test(...) per example below, in this order, named `Find Hazards example <n>`; then at most twelve tests of your own on section 2.2 (hazardsUnordered.json, tiny.json for implicit-read). Write no file anywhere.
